s:
Consider the following as objectives of the New Science and Technology Policy, 2003 and state which is/are correctly stated, with the help of codes given below :
1. Optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
2. Development of innovative technologies.
3. Development of systems and technologies for mitigation and management of natural hazards.
4. Management of intellectual property.
Codes :
x: Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was launched on January 3, 2003, for expanding new dimensions of innovation and preparation of futuristic perspective of science and technology, during 90th National Science Congress in Bengaluru. The policy includes optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources, development of innovative technologies, development of system and technologies for mitigation and management of natural hazards and management of intellectual property etc.

s: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020?
x: Atal Innovation Mission was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students. ONOS and RIEF were associated with the draft policy proposals.

s: Who is the President of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
x: The Prime Minister is ANRF's President; the Ministers of S&T and Education are Vice-Presidents.

s: Which of the following is a role of State Councils of Science and Technology such as APCOST?
o: Issuing national patents and regulating all Union laboratories
Framing state science and technology policy, providing research grants and popularising science
Serving as the statutory governing council of ANRF
Determining India’s Global Innovation Index methodology
x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science. They do not perform the national statutory functions of ANRF or NITI Aayog.

s: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD once in how many years?
x: Draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling FTE researchers, GERD and private GERD share every five years.

s: The STI Policy, 2013 aimed to place India among the top how many scientific powers by 2020?
x: The STI Policy, 2013 made innovation central and aimed for India to be among the top five scientific powers by 2020.

s: To what level did the STI Policy, 2013 aim to raise India's share of global publications from 3.5%?
x: It aimed to raise the share from 3.5% to over 7% and to quadruple papers in the top 1% journals.

s: The STI Policy, 2013 envisaged STI intervention in about how many high-impact sectors?
x: The 2013 policy envisaged STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors.

s: What did the vision of the Draft STIP 2020 include?
o: A regional scientific power only by 2050
Dependent on the top three foreign research systems
The sole scientific superpower within five years
One of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade
x: The Draft STIP 2020 envisioned India becoming one of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade and proposed a people-centric STI ecosystem.

s: For which body did the Draft STIP 2020 propose hybrid funding from private capital and CSR?
x: Draft STIP 2020 proposed a National Research Foundation with hybrid funding; the STI Development Bank was a corpus fund for long-term strategic areas.

s: One Nation, One Subscription was proposed in which policy?
x: One Nation, One Subscription came from the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved in 2024; it was not part of the STI Policy, 2013.

s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for improving India’s Global Innovation Index rank and also publishes the India Innovation Index?
x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.

s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Science and Technology Policy, 2003?
o: Promotion of research, innovation and technology transfer
Placing India among the top five scientific powers by 2020
Optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources
x: The top-five-scientific-powers-by-2020 aim belongs to the STI Policy, 2013; the other three were 2003 objectives.

s: The National Innovation Council, established in 2010, was associated with which of the following?
o: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and the management of defence production
Sam Pitroda and the promotion of inclusive innovation
The Principal Scientific Adviser and the regulation of higher education
NITI Aayog and the preparation of the Five Year Plans
x: The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.

x: The RDI Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore works through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF to boost private R&D; Rs 20,000 crore was provided for FY 2025-26.

s: On which date was the Science and Technology Policy, 2003 launched?
x: The S&T Policy, 2003 was launched on 3 January 2003.

s: Which body set up the Atal Innovation Mission in 2016?

s: In which year was India's Technology Policy Statement issued?
x: The sequence is SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003 and STI Policy 2013.

s: India's Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) reached what share of GDP in FY 2023-24, described as a 15-year high?
x: GERD reached 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24, a 15-year high. About 0.64-0.65% was the earlier level, 2% is the national target that every policy has missed, and 1.2% is not a recorded level.

s: Which policy aimed to raise GERD to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan?
x: The S&T Policy, 2003 set the 2% of GDP GERD target for the end of the Tenth Plan; the 2013 policy repeated 2% with private spending matching public.

s: What is the name of the unified fellowship proposed in the 2026 recommendations on research funding?

s: Which two policies set no numeric GERD target?
x: The 1958 Resolution and 1983 Statement had no numeric GERD target; the 2% target came with STP 2003.

Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants is situated at which of the following place?
x: Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (CIMAP) is a premier multidisciplinary research institute of Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) with its major focus on exploiting the potential of medicinal and aromatic plants (MAPs) by cultivation, bioprospection, chemical characterization, extraction, and formulation of bioactive phytomolecules. It is situated at Lucknow. Initially set up as Central Indian Medicinal Plants Organisation (CIMPO) in the year 1957 with a mandate to work and stimulate research on medicinal plants; subsequently aromatic plants also brought under its ambit. CIMPO started functioning from 26th March, 1959 and rechristened as Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (CIMAP) in the year 1978.

s: When and where was the Central Electrochemical Research Institute established with the efforts of Alagappa Chettiar, Dr. Shanti Swaroop Bhatnagar and Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru?
x: Central Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI), founded in 1948, has its roots in the patriotic fervor of Dr. R.M. Alagappa Chettiar, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr. Shanthi Swarup Bhatnagar. On January 14, 1953 CECRI became a physical reality when Dr. S. Radhakrishnan dedicated CECRI in Karaikudi (Tamil Nadu), the twelfth national laboratory under the CSIR, to the nation. CECRI represents the largest research establishment for electrochemistry in South Asia, Headquartered at Karaikudi, CECRI has extension centers in Chennai, Mandapam and Tuticorin.
